title: Aircraft Welder (GySgt to LCpl) NMOS (6092), DC AVN
raw_text:
12.     MOS 6043, Aircraft Welder (GySgt to LCpl) NMOS (6092), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aircraft Welders fabricate and repair aircraft metals
through basic welding using the gas/tungsten/titanium welding/arc/welding
(GTAW) process on aluminum alloys, steel alloys, stainless steel alloys, and
precipitating hardening nickel-based alloys.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Possess PMOS 6092.

            (2) Must have normal color perception.

            (3) Must have vision better than 20/30.

            (4) Must have normal depth perception.

            (5) Completed the Training and Readiness 4000 SSSP for PMOS 6092.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Must complete one of the following:

            (a) Aircraft/Support Equipment Basic Welding Certification Course
(N-701-0007) (M0464QE).

            (b) Oxyfuel/Shielded Metal Arc Welding Certification Course (N-
701-0009) (M04685E).

        (2) Previously qualified individuals who need to recertify per
reference (ad) COMNAVFORINST 4790.2 must complete one of the following:

            (a) Aircraft/Support Equipment Basic Welding Recertification
Course (N-701-0008) (M0464QE).

            (b) Oxyfuel/Shielded Metal Arc Welder Recertification Course (N-
701-0010) (M04685E).

        (3) The local administrative organization will assign MOS 6043 via
unit diary upon review of the Marine's graduation certificate from one of the
listed courses.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ad) COMNAVFORINST 4790.2 and (bn) 4790.1.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Welders, Cutters, Soldiers, and Brazers 51-4121.



                                         3-361                       Enclosure (1)
 3138                                                                   NAVMC 1200.1L



       f.   Related Military Skill.     Metal Worker, 1316.
common_text: The Aircraft Maintenance OccFlds includes direct and indirect support of the total airframes and power plant package of all aviation aircraft weapons systems. While there is similarity in the skills required to provide this support, the systems being supported are diverse.. The following examples are provided: direct support-repair and servicing at the organizational maintenance activity which is normally accomplished on aircraft, e.g., preflight and servicing of aircraft and their systems; indirect support-repair of components at the intermediate maintenance activity which is normally accomplished off aircraft, e.g., hydraulic actuators, servos, and accumulators, aircraft engines, and transmissions. Marines entering these fields receive MOS 6000, Basic Aircraft Maintenance Marine, and then progress through specific hard skill MOSs. After completion of formal training, Marines are qualified to maintain airframes and aircraft components. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of a Department of Labor Certification of Apprenticeship Completion maybe available in some MOSs within OccFlds 60/61/ 62. As the Marine progresses, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is placed in a management/supervisory position. Billets for both repair and administration are varied and extend from the squadron level to staff positions at the wing, force commander, and Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps level.

The Aircraft Maintenance OccFlds includes direct and indirect support of the total airframes and power plant package of all aviation aircraft weapons systems. While there is similarity in the skills required to provide this support, the systems being supported are diverse.. The following examples are provided: direct support-repair and servicing at the organizational maintenance activity which is normally accomplished on aircraft, e.g., preflight and servicing of aircraft and their systems; indirect support-repair of components at the intermediate maintenance activity which is normally accomplished off aircraft, e.g., hydraulic actuators, servos, and accumulators, aircraft engines, and transmissions. Marines entering these fields receive MOS 6000, Basic Aircraft Maintenance Marine, and then progress through specific hard skill MOSs. After completion of formal training, Marines are qualified to maintain airframes and aircraft components. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of a Department of Labor Certification of Apprenticeship Completion maybe available in some MOSs within OccFlds 60/61/ 62. As the Marine progresses, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is placed in a management/supervisory position. Billets for both repair and administration are varied and extend from the squadron level to staff positions at the wing, force commander, and Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps level.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
